Title: Placement-only commerce metrics change when date_axis=event_date (Core says they are 'identical on both axes')
Evidence: 1 metrics affected: default. `orders` last7 None (default) vs None (event_date); last30 None vs None (+55%). ClickHouse reproduces it: orders placed in last30 = 1006; sale orders having any outcome event in the window = 1557 (551 are older orders).
Cause / why it matters: Root cause: `fact_orders` joins `order_events` one-to-many; with an event_date filter the join admits every older order that had a cancel/RTO/return that day, and `orders`/`new_customers`/`total_sales` etc. count them. Because event_date is the default axis, the agent's 'orders 45' on 2026-10-24 (real: 26 placed) and AOV, COD, new-customer figures are inflated whenever the event-date axis is on.
Repro: Repro: metrics_query(measure='orders', time_range=2026-10-24..2026-10-24, date_axis='event_date') -> 45; same without date_axis -> 26. Expected: 26 on both axes, or a refusal.
Proposed fix: Fix (Core): for placement_only/cohort_only metrics ignore date_axis and drop the order_events join, or refuse with a reason. Interim fix (agent repo, needs your OK): do not forward date_axis for metrics whose catalogue date_axis is placement_only/cohort_only/native.
Status: FIXED in working trees (not committed, not deployed): Core planner no longer swaps placement_only metrics to commerce.event_date (+ test); agent no longer forwards date_axis for non-switchable measures (+ tests). Redeploy Core to take effect. Mixed switchable + placement-only calls still send the axis.

Title: 29 procurement / inventory / vendor metrics are refused as 'stale_data' although the pipeline loaded them today
Evidence: Examples: po_count (purchase_orders latest_data_at 2026-10-16, 'days_behind 10'), vendor_count (2026-10-19, 7 days), qc_count (10-24), received_units (10-24). Raw Iceberg for the same objects was extracted 2026-10-26 07:14 UTC and gold loaded 07:26 UTC. Metrics: avg_actual_lead_days, avg_planned_lead_days, line_fill_rate, line_ordered_units, line_received_units, line_value, open_purchase_orders, overdue_purchase_orders, po_count, po_fill_rate, po_lines, po_ordered_units, po_received_units, po_value, qc_actual_units, qc_count, qc_damage_rate, qc_damage_units, qc_damage_value, qc_invoice_units, qc_shortfall_rate, qc_shortfall_units, receipt_layers, received_units, received_value, rejected_quality_checks, remaining_units, remaining_value, vendor_count
Cause / why it matters: The gate compares the max business date of a sparse transactional table (last PO date / last vendor update) with 'allowed_lag_days: 1'. A quiet week looks like a stalled pipeline, so the whole Procurement/Inventory domain is unavailable to the agent. Checked: serve.purchase_requests has orders to 2026-10-22 while the gate reports 10-16, so the gate's date source also needs checking. For stock_layers the view itself is broken - see B-13.
Proposed fix: Use pipeline load time (max _loaded_at / refreshed_at) for the freshness SLA, or a per-view exemption for sparse tables.
Status: Open - needs a policy decision. Not edited: options are (a) probe a load-time column instead of the business date, (b) per-view cadence exemption for sparse tables, (c) fail-open with a warning.
